correctness.rationale: For the corrected statement: translate one frequency to zero; orthogonality is vanishing of the cubic mask at all nonzero differences. Positivity excludes phase zero and reality and degree allow only a real zero −1, a conjugate unit pair, or both. A triangle using conjugate nonreal phases forces z³=1 or z²=−1 with −1 also a root. In a triangle using −1 and a nonreal z, the third difference forces −z to be the conjugate of z, again giving ±i. The third-root factorization gives b=c=a+d, and the fourth-root factorization gives uniform masses. Four orthogonal columns also force uniformity by row norms and their residues, after translation, are 0,1/4,1/2,3/4 modulo 1. For pairs, P(−1)=0 or the quadratic factor z²−2tz+1 gives t=(d−b)/(2a), d(d−b)=a(a−c), and the required strict |t|<1. The frozen line 20 said 'every maximal'; at masses (1,2,2,1)/6, phases 0 and 1/2 already form an inclusion-maximal pair, not an optimal triple. The scope already intended maximum cardinality; the supplied replacement RESULT.md makes that restriction explicit, supplies the counterexample to the broader reading and fixes the modulus typo in Step 4, without changing the capacity formula.
residual_risks: The all-real proof, not the packaged finite numerical root check, establishes the result. The checker currently imports only the standard library despite the frozen verification description mentioning SymPy and NumPy.

value.rationale: The maximum number of exact mutually orthogonal weighted Fourier samples is a natural invariant even without a full basis. All four possibilities are realized, and the exact phase obstruction explains why the planar positive-square capacities cannot just be reused for equally spaced samples. In particular the pair locus and unique optimum triple after translation answer structural questions across all positive weights, rather than checking isolated examples.
residual_risks: No claim beyond strictly positive weights on four consecutive sites or their affine images.
